front: Trend in atomic radius across Period 3
back: Decreases Na → Cl: nuclear charge rises, shielding almost constant, outer electrons pulled closer.
Na⁺, Mg²⁺, Al³⁺ (2 shells) small and decreasing; P³⁻, S²⁻, Cl⁻ (3 shells) large and decreasing.

front: Dips in first IE across Period 3
back: Al < Mg (3p electron, higher energy, shielded by 3s). S < P (paired 3p electron repels).
Silicon: giant covalent lattice, many strong Si–Si bonds broken on melting.

front: Melting points of P₄, S₈, Cl₂, Ar
back: Order S₈ > P₄ > Cl₂ > Ar: more electrons per particle, stronger instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces.
More delocalised electrons per atom, higher charge and smaller cations: stronger bonding, higher melting point and conductivity.
Na, Mg, Al conduct (Al best); Si semiconductor (rises when warmed); P, S, Cl, Ar insulators.
The repeating pattern of physical and chemical properties across successive periods.
Na, Mg, Al giant metallic; Si giant covalent; P₄, S₈, Cl₂ simple molecular; Ar monatomic.
